svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.20.6.3 Thickness of Interior Walls
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.20 MASONRY AND INSULATING CONCRETE FORM WALLS NOT IN CONTACT WITH THE GROUND
Thickness of Interior Walls

g.text: Loadbearing: spacing of supports not more
apart need a wall at least 2 700 / 20 =
times the thickness, and the wall not
apart need a wall at least 2 700 / 36 =

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
The thickness of loadbearing interior walls is
determined from the maximum lateral support
spacing in Sentences 9.20.10.1.(2) and (3).
The thickness of interior non-loadbearing
walls is
(a) determined from the maximum lateral support
spacing in Sentences 9.20.10.1.(2) and (3), and
(b) in any case not less than 65 mm (2 9/16″).
Supports are spaced not more than 20 times the
wall thickness for all loadbearing walls and
exterior non-loadbearing walls, and 36 times the
thickness for interior non-loadbearing walls.
Supports are floors, roofs, intersecting masonry
walls or buttresses.
Drawn: walls supported top and bottom by floor framing. Wall heights and the examples are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.20.6.3. (page 9-142)
